segments.t: At the ASK agency, Catherine Barneville drops by to visit Noemie, who is wearing a neck brace. When Mathias arrives, Catherine reveals she has invited Noemie over for dinner with her handsome physical therapist. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Catherine, tu voulais me voir?
Non mon chéri, je viens voir Noémie.
Elle porte un corset depuis quinze jours.
Oui, elle doit bien se reposer.
Je la trouve vraiment très rayonnante.
C'est gentil d'être passée à l'agence.
Je l'ai invitée à dîner ce soir.
Tu l'as invitée chez nous?
Oui, avec quelques amis très sympathiques.
Mon kiné Alexandre sera là aussi.
Tu penses que c'est une bonne idée?
Il est charmant et extrêmement doué.
Il va beaucoup l'aider pour sa rééducation.
D'accord, nous verrons bien ce soir.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Catherine, tu voulais me voir?
'Catherine, did you want to see me?' Mathias asks his wife about her visit. The imperfect 'you' inquires about her intention.
Non mon chéri, je viens voir Noémie.
'No my darling, I am visiting Noemie.' Catherine explains she came to see Noemie. The affectionate term 'my' addresses her husband.
Elle porte un corset depuis quinze jours.
'She has been wearing a brace for two weeks.' Catherine notes Noemie's neck brace. The verb 'porter' means to wear.
Oui, elle doit bien se reposer.
'Yes, she needs to rest properly.' Mathias agrees on the necessity of recovery. The modal verb 'must' expresses an obligation.
Je la trouve vraiment très rayonnante.
'I find her truly very radiant.' Catherine compliments Noemie's healthy appearance. The feminine adjective 'rayonnante' describes someone looking bright and well.
C'est gentil d'être passée à l'agence.
'It is kind of you to stop by the agency.' Mathias acknowledges her visit politely. The adjective 'kind' expresses appreciation.
Je l'ai invitée à dîner ce soir.
'I invited her to dinner tonight.' Catherine announces the dinner invitation. The passe compose 'j'ai invitee' shows agreement with the preceding direct object.
Tu l'as invitée chez nous?
'You invited her to our place?' Mathias reacts with nervous surprise. The prepositional phrase 'at the home of' means at our home.
Oui, avec quelques amis très sympathiques.
'Yes, with a few very nice friends.' Catherine describes the guest list. The indefinite determiner 'a few' introduces plural nouns.
Mon kiné Alexandre sera là aussi.
'My physiotherapist Alexandre will be there too.' Catherine mentions her physical therapist. The noun 'physiotherapist' is a colloquial short form for kinesitherapeute.
Tu penses que c'est une bonne idée?
'Do you think that is a good idea?' Mathias questions the matchmaking scheme. The verb phrase 'a' questions her initiative.
Il est charmant et extrêmement doué.
'He is charming and extremely talented.' Catherine praises Alexandre's qualities. The adverb 'extremement' intensifies the adjective 'doue'.
Il va beaucoup l'aider pour sa rééducation.
'He will help her a lot with her rehabilitation.' Catherine justifies the match with therapeutic benefits. The noun 'rehabilitation' refers to physical therapy.
D'accord, nous verrons bien ce soir.

'Okay, we shall see tonight.' Mathias concedes with quiet hesitation. The simple future 'we' anticipates the outcome. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

Il est charmant et extrêmement doué.

Mathias looks uneasy as Catherine departs after organizing the unexpected dinner party. Bringing Noemie and her new physiotherapist under the same roof promises an awkward evening. Now, let's review the scene once more.
